mainTopic: What wording makes a person a נזיר: 'birds,' and vowing from just one prohibition
overview: The משנה taught that if someone says 'I take upon myself birds,' רבי מאיר says he is a נזיר, and the חכמים say he is not. ריש לקיש explains that, for רבי מאיר, a person ties his words to what sits next to them in the פסוק, and the רבנן disagree. רבי יוחנן says everyone rejects that idea. In his view, רבי מאיר is worried the man meant the birds an impure נזיר brings. The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן against three other readings of 'birds' by looking at the man's wording and at the pure נזיר passing in front of him. It then shows where the two explanations really differ: someone who explicitly says 'the birds next to hair' when no נזיר is around. A challenge from saying 'ימין' (right hand) as a שבועה is turned away, because 'right hand' is an oath word on its own. A new משנה rules that vowing נזירות from even one item, like grape seeds or shaving, makes a person a full נזיר. The גמרא says this does not follow רבי שמעון, who requires a vow from all the items, and gives each side's פסוק. It then begins asking which 'wine of a מצוה' רבי שמעון forbids to a נזיר.

steps.title: The Rabbis' side of ריש לקיש's explanation
steps.stepSummary: Finishing ריש לקיש's explanation: the רבנן hold that a person does not tie his vow to something that only sits next to it in a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis hold: a person does not connect his words to something that is placed next to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes ריש לקיש's explanation of the argument by stating the view of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, רבי מאיר holds that a person can tie his words to something placed next to it in the פסוק. The רבנן disagree. Saying 'birds' does not pull in a nearby topic, so the speaker did not mean נזירות and he is not a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (the חכמים of the משנה)
Attaches / connects his vow to something
That is placed right next to it (in the פסוק)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
phrases.notes: This is still ריש לקיש talking. He explains both sides of the argument in the משנה.

phrases.english: a person does not connect his vow
to something that is placed next to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's two-sided explanation, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן reject tying a vow to a nearby topic, so the speaker is not a נזיר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's different reason for רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says everyone agrees a person does not tie his vow to a nearby topic. רבי מאיר's reason is a worry that the man meant the birds of an impure נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: everyone agrees that a person does not connect his vow to something nearby. Rather, this is רבי מאיר's reason: we are worried that perhaps he took upon himself the birds of an impure נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects ריש לקיש's explanation and gives a new reason for רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the argument is not about tying words to nearby topics, since everyone agrees about that. A נזיר who becomes impure must bring two birds as a קרבן. So when a person says 'birds,' רבי מאיר worries he meant to become a נזיר who would bring those birds if he became impure.

keyTerms.meaning: We are worried / we take into account the possibility
A נזיר who became impure (from a dead body)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the man definitely meant נזירות. He only says we are 'worried' he might have, so we treat him as a נזיר. That word 'worried' is exactly what the next step questions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone agrees one does not connect his vow to it.
Rather, this is the reason of Rabbi Meir:
that we are worried that perhaps
he took upon himself the birds of an impure nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֲמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא מַתְפֵּיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש and offers a different reason for רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר makes him a נזיר out of concern that 'birds' meant the birds of an impure נזיר.

steps.title: Maybe he meant voluntary bird offerings
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוחנן only says 'we are worried,' perhaps the man meant voluntary birds and not נזירות at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he said 'we are worried,' maybe he took upon himself birds as a voluntary gift offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. If it is only a worry, there is another easy way to read the man's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can promise birds as a voluntary עולה (a נדבה). That has nothing to do with נזירות. If that reading is possible, why should we make him a נזיר?

keyTerms.meaning: Birds brought as a voluntary gift offering

phrases.english: Since he said "we are worried,"
perhaps he took upon himself birds as a gift offering?

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that we worry the man meant an impure נזיר's birds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another reading of 'birds' is just as likely: a voluntary offering. So there is no reason to assume נזירות.

steps.title: A voluntary offering has its own wording
steps.stepSummary: If he meant a voluntary offering, he would have said 'הרי עלי קן' (a nest).
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should have said 'I take upon myself a nest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the man's wording shows he did not mean a voluntary bird offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual way to promise voluntary birds is to say 'a קן' (a pair of birds). He said 'birds' instead. That change in wording points away from a נדבה and toward the birds of a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'nest': the normal word for a pair of bird offerings

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, ״הֲרֵי עָלַי קֵן״ מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: If so, he should have said: "It is upon me to bring a nest."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, ״הֲרֵי עָלַי קֵן״ מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about a voluntary offering.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording proof: he did not use the normal phrase for a gift offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Birds' could just mean a voluntary bird offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: A voluntary offering would be phrased 'קן,' so 'birds' points elsewhere.

steps.title: Maybe he meant a מצורע's birds
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps he was promising the birds that a מצורע brings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he meant: 'I take upon myself the birds of a מצורע'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another possible meaning of 'birds.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע also needs birds for his purification (ויקרא 14:4). So 'birds' could mean he is taking on the birds for a מצורע, not birds of נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: The birds used in purifying a מצורע

phrases.english: But perhaps "It is upon me
to bring the birds of a leper" is what he meant?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the voluntary-offering reading is set aside, a new alternative reading is raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that 'birds' refers to נזירות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מצורע's birds are another known bird obligation, so the man's words could mean those.

steps.title: A נזיר was passing in front of him
steps.stepSummary: The case is when a נזיר was walking by, so the man clearly had נזירות in mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where a נזיר was passing in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case. רבי מאיר is talking about a situation where a נזיר was passing by.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setting tells us what he was thinking about. With a נזיר right in front of him, 'birds' points to נזיר birds and not a מצורע's.

keyTerms.meaning: For example / it is a case where

phrases.english: It is a case where a nazirite was passing before him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מצורע challenge by defining the setting.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a specific setting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Birds' might refer to a מצורע's birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נזיר passing by shows he was thinking about נזירות.

steps.title: Maybe he meant to pay for that impure נזיר's birds
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the passing נזיר was impure, and the man only meant to pay for that נזיר's bird offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it was an impure נזיר, and he meant to free him from his offerings by bringing them for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Seeing a נזיר could lead to a different kind of promise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the passing נזיר was impure, he owes birds. The man might have meant 'I will bring that נזיר's birds for him,' which does not make the speaker himself a נזיר.

phrases.english: But perhaps it was an impure nazirite,
and he meant to exempt him from his offerings?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא נָזִיר טָמֵא, וּלְפוֹטְרוֹ מִן קׇרְבְּנוֹתָיו קָאָמַר
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a passing נזיר proves the man meant to become a נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A passing impure נזיר owes birds, so the man may have offered to cover that נזיר's obligation rather than take on נזירות.

steps.title: The passing נזיר was pure
steps.stepSummary: The case is when a pure נזיר was passing, who owes no birds, so the man must mean birds for his own נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where a pure נזיר was passing in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by making the case even more exact: the נזיר passing by was pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pure נזיר does not owe birds, so there is nothing of his to pay for. The only sensible meaning left is that the speaker is taking נזירות on himself, along with the birds he would owe if he became impure. This keeps רבי יוחנן's explanation of רבי מאיר standing.

keyTerms.meaning: A pure נזיר, who owes no bird offerings

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי מאיר makes the speaker a נזיר because 'birds' likely means an impure נזיר's birds. The גמרא defends this step by step. It is not a voluntary offering, because that would be called a 'קן.' It is not a מצורע's birds, because a נזיר was passing by. It is not paying for another נזיר's birds, because the passing נזיר was pure.

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה נָזִיר טָהוֹר עוֹבֵר לְפָנָיו.
phrases.english: It is a case where a pure nazirite was passing before him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה נָזִיר טָהוֹר עוֹבֵר לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the impure-נזיר challenge by narrowing the case further.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He may have meant to pay for a passing impure נזיר's birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The passing נזיר was pure and owed nothing, so the speaker meant his own נזירות.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two opinions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, since in the end both seem to need a נזיר passing by. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-8 limited רבי יוחנן's explanation to a case where a נזיר was passing by. In the משנה's plain case of saying 'birds,' both explanations seem to need that setting, so the two opinions look the same in practice. The גמרא wants to find a case where they would rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?
רבי שמעון בן לקיש; he explains רבי מאיר's ruling through the birds being next to hair in the פסוק

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, who each explained רבי מאיר's ruling differently.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 limited the case to a passing pure נזיר, both opinions seem the same, so the גמרא asks what separates them.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש would rule differently.

steps.title: They differ when he says "the birds next to hair"
steps.stepSummary: If someone says "the birds placed next to hair are on me": for רבי יוחנן it is נזירות only if a נזיר is passing by, and for ריש לקיש it is נזירות even with no נזיר present.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when he said, "The birds that are next to hair are on me." According to רבי יוחנן, even though he said this, if a נזיר was passing before him, yes, it is נזירות; if not, no. According to רבי שמעון בן לקיש, it is נזירות even if no נזיר was passing before him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a case where the two opinions really split: the man says "the birds next to hair" when no נזיר is around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, רבי מאיר holds that a person's words connect to what sits next to them in the פסוק. So clearly naming the birds next to hair is enough to make him a נזיר. According to רבי יוחנן, everyone agrees that this connection does not count, and only a passing נזיר shows what he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The birds placed next to hair: the bird offerings that appear near the shaving of hair in the פרשה of נזיר
A נזיר passing in front of him

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, רבי מאיר needs a passing נזיר to show what the man meant. According to ריש לקיש, רבי מאיר holds that a person ties his words to what sits next to them in a פסוק.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
in a case where he said:
"The birds that are next to hair are upon me,"
phrases.notes: In the פרשה of נזיר (במדבר 6), the impure נזיר's birds come right next to the shaving of his hair.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר הָכִי,
phrases.english: according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, even though he said this,
if a nazirite was passing before him, yes,
if not, no.
According to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאֵין נָזִיר עוֹבֵר לְפָנָיו.
phrases.english: even though no nazirite was passing before him.
phrases.notes: The words "it is still נזירות" are left out, but that's what he means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's question by naming a case where the two opinions split.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ when he explicitly says "birds next to hair" and no נזיר is present: ריש לקיש says it is נזירות, and רבי יוחנן says it is not.

steps.title: Does anyone really reject the "next to it" rule? The case of saying "right hand"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's position using a ברייתא: saying "ימין" is a שבועה, apparently because in a פסוק "right hand" appears next to swearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there really anyone who says a person does not tie his words to something placed next to it? But a ברייתא teaches: one who says "Right hand" has made a שבועה. What is the reason? Is it not because it is written, "He raised his right hand and his left hand to the heavens and swore by the One Who lives forever"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether anyone can reject the idea that a person ties his words to what sits next to them in a פסוק. It brings a ברייתא that seems to rely on exactly that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "right hand" is not obviously an oath word. The ברייתא still treats it as a שבועה, and the guess is that this is because a פסוק in דניאל puts "right hand" right next to swearing. If so, the "next to it" rule is accepted by everyone, which goes against both the רבנן in ריש לקיש's explanation and רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Ties or connects his vow to something
That is placed next to it

phrases.english: Is there anyone who says
that a person does not tie his vow
to something placed next to it?
phrases.notes: This is aimed at anyone who holds that view: the רבנן in ריש לקיש's explanation, and everyone in רבי יוחנן's.

phrases.english: But it is taught: one who says "Right hand" —
that is an oath.
What is the reason? Is it not because it is written:
"He raised his right hand and his left hand to the heavens
and swore by the One Who lives forever"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לָא מַתְפֵּיס אִינִישׁ בְּמִילְּתָא דִּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 10 showed that רבי יוחנן rejects the "next to it" rule; this step challenges whether anyone can reject it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a person does not tie his vow to something placed next to it in a פסוק. ריש לקיש gives this view to the רבנן, and רבי יוחנן says everyone holds it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes "ימין" a שבועה apparently only because it sits next to swearing in a פסוק. That shows the "next to it" rule is accepted by all.

steps.title: No, "right hand" is itself a name for an oath
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: "ימין" is a שבועה because the word itself means an oath, as learned from "נשבע ה׳ בימינו." Likewise, "left" comes from "ובזרוע עוזו."
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: No. It is because "right hand" itself is called an oath, as a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that one who says "right hand" has made a שבועה? Because it says, "ה׳ has sworn by His right hand." And from where do we know that one who says "left" has made a שבועה? Because it says, "and by the arm of His strength."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. "Right hand" counts as a שבועה because the word itself is used for swearing, not because it sits next to an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ישעיהו, ה׳ swears "by His right hand," so the right hand is itself what one swears by. The same פסוק adds "the arm of His strength," which is understood as the left. Since both words are oath words on their own, the ברייתא is no proof for the "next to it" rule, and רבי יוחנן's position stands.
steps.whatToRemember: "ימין" and "שמאל" are oath words in their own right. So this ברייתא does not prove that everyone accepts the "next to it" rule, and רבי יוחנן's opinion survives.

phrases.english: They say: No,
it is because "right hand" itself is called an oath.
As it is taught: From where do we know that one who says "Right hand"
has made an oath?
As it says: "ה׳ has sworn by His right hand."
And from where do we know that one who says "Left" has made an oath?
As it says: "And by the arm of His strength."
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק. The arm paired with the right hand is understood as the left.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא, מִשּׁוּם דְּיָמִין גּוּפֵיהּ אִיקְּרִי שְׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 11's proof by giving a different reason why "ימין" is a שבועה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not decide the dispute itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed "ימין" works only because it sits next to swearing in דניאל. In fact, the word is an oath term on its own, based on ישעיהו 62:8.

steps.title: Vowing to be a נזיר from just one prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who says he is a נזיר from grape seeds, grape skins, shaving, or טומאה becomes a full נזיר, and all the rules of נזירות apply to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says, 'I am a נזיר from grape seeds,' or 'from grape skins,' or 'from shaving,' or 'from becoming impure,' he is a נזיר, and all the details of נזירות are on him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that naming even one prohibition of a נזיר is enough to make a person a complete נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person mentioned only one item that a נזיר is forbidden in, yet the משנה does not limit him to that one item. He takes on the whole package: no wine or grape products, no haircut, and no טומאת מת.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity (here, from a dead body)
All the detailed rules of being a נזיר

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he is a נזיר only for the one thing he named. The משנה says he becomes a נזיר in every way.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
'I am hereby a nazir from grape seeds,'
or 'from grape skins,'
or 'from shaving,' or 'from impurity' —
he is a nazir,
and all the details of naziriteship are upon him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of indirect wordings of נזירות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Accepting נזירות by naming even one of its prohibitions makes a person a full נזיר with all of its rules.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון. A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון requires a vow covering all the prohibitions, while the רבנן say even one is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Our משנה is not like רבי שמעון. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says he is not obligated until he vows from all of them. The רבנן say: even if he vowed from only one of them, he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names who disagrees with the משנה and brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about this exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, someone who says only 'from grape seeds' would not become a נזיר at all. The משנה follows the רבנן, who say one item is enough. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא looks for each side's source.

keyTerms.meaning: Until he vows from all of them

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Our mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.
As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon says:
He is not obligated until he vows from all of them.
And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ לָא נְזַר אֶלָּא בְּחַד מִנְּהוֹן
phrases.english: Even if he vowed nazirite-style from only one of them,
he is a nazir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose view the משנה follows, and whose view it rejects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows the רבנן (one item is enough). רבי שמעון requires a vow that covers all the prohibitions.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's source verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns his view from the פסוק 'from all that is made of the grapevine, from seeds to skin.' This shows the vow must cover everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי שמעון's reason? The פסוק says: 'from all that is made of the grapevine, from seeds to skin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי שמעון's source and answers right away with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses 'from all,' covering the whole range from seeds to skins. רבי שמעון reads this to mean that נזירות takes effect only when the vow includes everything a נזיר is forbidden in.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?
The verse says:
'From all that is made of the grapevine,'
'from seeds to skin.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי שמעון's position from the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's rule that a vow must include all the prohibitions
steps.raayaSupportSource: 'מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין מחרצנים ועד זג' (במדבר 6:4)

steps.title: The Rabbis' source verse
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn their view from 'he shall abstain from wine and strong drink.' This shows that naming wine alone is enough to bring all the rules of נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what is their reason? The פסוק says: 'From wine and strong drink he shall abstain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's source, a different פסוק from the same section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק mentions only wine and strong drink, yet it describes the person as a נזיר. The רבנן learn that a vow naming just one part still brings on the full נזירות.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, what is their reason?
The verse says: 'From wine and strong drink he shall abstain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 15: gives the other side's source.
steps.raayaObject: The רבנן's rule that vowing from one item is enough

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון do with the Rabbis' verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון: the פסוק 'from wine and strong drink he shall abstain' is written in the Torah, so how does he deal with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמעון also has this פסוק written: 'From wine and strong drink he shall abstain'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי שמעון, because the רבנן's פסוק is in the Torah for him too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this פסוק shows that naming wine alone is enough, then רבי שמעון must either accept that reading or explain what else the פסוק teaches. The challenge forces him to give the פסוק another job.

phrases.english: And for Rabbi Shimon too,
isn't it written: 'From wine and strong drink he shall abstain'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון using the רבנן's פסוק from step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק the רבנן rely on exists for רבי שמעון too, so he should agree with their reading unless he uses it for something else.

steps.title: רבי שמעון uses the verse for מצוה wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון needs that פסוק for a different lesson: a נזיר is forbidden to drink wine used for a מצוה, just like ordinary wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that פסוק to forbid wine of a מצוה, just like optional wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון uses the פסוק to teach something else, so it is not available to prove the רבנן's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think wine drunk for a מצוה is allowed to a נזיר. רבי שמעון learns from this פסוק that it is forbidden like any other wine. Since the פסוק is used for this lesson, it does not teach that naming one item is enough.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows the רבנן: naming even one prohibition makes a person a full נזיר. רבי שמעון requires all of them, and he uses 'מיין ושכר יזיר' to forbid even מצוה wine to a נזיר.

phrases.english: He needs that verse
to forbid wine of a מצוה just like optional wine.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The פסוק is needed for a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מיין ושכר יזיר' teaches that a vow naming one item is enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי שמעון, the פסוק teaches that a נזיר is forbidden even in wine used for a מצוה.

steps.title: Which wine counts as wine of a מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'wine of a מצוה' means and suggests it is the wine used for קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this 'wine of a מצוה'? Is it the wine of קידוש and הבדלה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to pin down exactly which wine רבי שמעון meant in Step 18, and offers the obvious guess: the wine of קידוש and הבדלה. This question is setting up the next move in the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said a נזיר may not drink wine used for a מצוה, but it never said which wine. The גמרא now names a specific case, קידוש and הבדלה, so it can test whether רבי שמעון's lesson really fits that case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A question asking for the exact meaning of something just mentioned.
קידוש, the blessing said over wine at the start of שבת and יום טוב.
הבדלה, the blessing said over wine when שבת and יום טוב end.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet a final answer. The גמרא is only suggesting what 'wine of a מצוה' might be, so keep reading to see whether this suggestion holds up.

phrases.english: What is it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the 'wine of a מצוה' from the last step, which רבי שמעון says a נזיר may not drink.

phrases.english: Is it the wine of kiddush and havdala?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact meaning of 'wine of a מצוה' from רבי שמעון's lesson in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which wine counts as 'wine of a מצוה' that a נזיר is forbidden to drink, according to רבי שמעון's reading of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question itself suggests the wine of קידוש and הבדלה. The גמרא's response comes on the next amud.
